course: Rewind to any step. Let another agent take it from there.

action_says: The action in `attach/` imports the bundle, checks the log's hash chain (against `head:` too, if you pin one), writes the session's export page and uploads it as a workflow artifact, then posts one comment on the pull request with the chain result, the number of secrets replaced and the download link.
A later push updates that comment instead of adding another.
Secrets are always replaced in the page; the action has no input to turn that off.
It installs `rewindagents` from the same commit as the action, so pinning the action's SHA pins the tool.
The token is handed to the comment step only.
If the log does not verify, the page is uploaded with its notice, and then the job fails.
It has not run on GitHub yet.
attach: rewindagents bundle --out .rewindagents-pr.bundle   # the session behind this change, secrets replaced
attach_says: The `.rewindagents/` store is git-ignored, so the checkout holds no log of its own; commit a bundle.
attach_yaml: pull-requests: write   # for the one comment; nothing else writes

agents: rewindagents install --agent codex      # adds the hook to .codex/hooks.json in this project
rewindagents install --agent cursor     # adds the hook to .cursor/hooks.json in this project
rewindagents install --agent cursor --settings ~/.cursor/hooks.json   # or for every project
export: rewindagents export --session abc --out replay.html  # a given session, to a given file
rewindagents export --no-contents                    # steps, tools and paths only: no inputs, results or diffs
rewindagents export --no-redact                      # keep secrets as recorded (they are replaced by default)
hook: rewindagents install            # adds the hook to .claude/settings.json in this project
rewindagents install --settings ~/.claude/settings.json   # or for every project
install: pipx install git+https://github.com/Johnbjoseph-cybersec/rewindagents     # or: pip install git+https://...
quick: pipx install git+https://github.com/Johnbjoseph-cybersec/rewindagents && cd your-project && rewindagents init
record: rewindagents verify     # OK: 1 records, chain intact
replay: rewindagents replay              # one line per step: number, tool, file or command
rewindagents replay --step 12    # step 12 in full: input, checkpoints, result
rewindagents diff 12             # the same files, as a unified diff: now -> step 12
rewindagents diff 12 src/db.py   # only that file (a directory means every file under it)
rewindagents rewind 12           # files back to how they were right after step 12
rewindagents rewind 12 --only src/db.py --only tests/   # put back only these
rewindagents revert 12 --dry-run # what taking back step 12 alone would change
rewindagents revert 12           # take back step 12 alone, keep every later step and hand edit
rewindagents branch 12 --name try2   # keep the current files, then rewind to step 12
sessions: rewindagents sessions                     # every session in the log: id, first and last time, steps, files touched
rewindagents sessions --grep config.py    # only sessions with a step that mentions it, and those steps
ui: rewindagents ui                      # opens the timeline in your browser; Ctrl+C stops it

bundle: rewindagents bundle --out s1.bundle                 # the latest session, and the file copies it names, in one file
rewindagents bundle --session abc --out abc.bundle  # a given session
rewindagents bundle --no-redact --out s1.bundle     # carry secrets as recorded (they are replaced by default)
rewindagents import s1.bundle                       # in another clone: check the file, then add the session to its log
bundle_says: Then `replay`, `rewind` and `branch` work on that session in the other clone, with `--session <id>`.
By default, secrets are replaced in the records and the stored copies, as `export` replaces them.

`import` writes nothing until everything checks out: the file's own SHA-256, every record's hash, that every record belongs to the session and is in log order, every stored copy against its SHA-256, that no copy a record names is missing, that this project's log verifies, and that it does not already hold the session.
Nothing goes over a network; carry the file however you like.
compare_says: Back in the project, `rewindagents compare` lines up the project and every run forked from the same step: per run, the agents and their number of tool calls since the start, the files changed, created or deleted and the lines added and removed; per file, which runs ended with the same bytes (the same letter).
`rewindagents compare --check "python3 -m pytest -q"` runs your command in each run and reports pass or the exit code, with the last lines of a failing one.
`rewindagents compare --diff proj try2` prints how two runs differ as a git diff (`git apply` in the first turns its files into the second's).
fork: rewindagents replay                         # pick the step to start from, say 12
rewindagents fork 12 --name try2            # ../<project>-try2 with step 12's files
cd ../your-project-try2                     # run any agent with a hook here, or edit by hand
rewindagents compare --diff your-project try2   # how two runs differ, as a git diff
facts.fork_lead: Rewind to any step, fork it, let another agent take it from there, compare.
fork_limits: `fork` refuses a step it cannot rebuild exactly (a stored copy missing, a command whose scan did not finish, a log that does not verify) and leaves nothing behind when it fails half-way.
`compare` writes nothing; the command `--check` runs may write in the run it runs in.
Runs from different steps are not mixed.
fork_says: A recorded step is a starting point you can hand to another agent, another model, another prompt or a person, and the runs that follow can be compared on what they actually did to the files and on your own check.

`rewindagents fork 12 --name try2` makes a new directory next to the project (`<project>-try2`; `--dir` picks another place outside it) holding the project's files as `rewind 12` would leave them: the project as it is now, with every change that session made after step 12 taken back, untracked files included.
In a git repository it is a `git worktree` on the branch `rewindagents/run/try2`, so your `HEAD`, index and files stay as they were; elsewhere it is a plain directory.

Run any agent there, or edit by hand: with a hook in place (the project's agent config comes along when git does not ignore it, or a `--global` hook), its steps go into the run's own log, and `replay`, `rewind` and `diff` work in the run as in any project.
gc: rewindagents gc --dry-run   # what would be deleted, and how many bytes
rewindagents gc --drop-pending-older-than 7   # first drop scans whose command never finished
gc_says: `gc` deletes every stored copy that no log record (in any session) and no pending scan (a command whose after-scan has not run) names, and prints how many it deleted and the bytes those files took on disk.
Every step of every session in the log can still be rewound afterwards; the copies a rewind needs are the ones the log names.
It refuses to run when the log does not verify, and it never writes to the log.

A scan whose after-scan never ran (the agent was killed, a crash) stays pending and keeps its copies; `--drop-pending-older-than DAYS` removes the scans older than DAYS first, so their copies are collected too.
Scans younger than 1 day are never dropped.
init_says: `init` looks for the agents it supports (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Copilot CLI, Droid, Qwen Code): their config directory in the project or your home directory, or their command on `PATH`.
It prints the plan, asks `[y/N]`, and adds the hook to each one it found, one line per agent: `installed`, `already there`, `replaced` or `not found`.
It never adds a second copy and keeps every hook already in the file.
`--global` writes each agent's user config instead, so every project is recorded.
Without `--yes` and without a terminal to ask on, it only prints the plan.
`--agent claude` sets up only that agent (repeat it for more).

In a git repository the config files `init` creates are listed in `.git/info/exclude`, this clone's own ignore list, because they name this machine's Python and would not run on a teammate's; a file git already tracks is changed and named instead.
`rewindagents init --undo` takes it all out again and keeps what was recorded.
more_agents: rewindagents install --agent gemini     # adds the hook to .gemini/settings.json in this project
rewindagents install --agent copilot    # adds the hook to .github/hooks/rewindagents.json in this repository
rewindagents install --agent droid      # adds the hook to .factory/settings.json (or .factory/hooks.json if it exists)
rewindagents install --agent qwen       # adds the hook to .qwen/settings.json in this project
rewindagents uninstall --agent qwen     # same flags as install, for every agent
quick_use: rewindagents summary                   # what it changed: each file, lines added and removed, which steps
rewindagents replay                    # what it did, one line per step
rewindagents diff 12                   # what taking it back to step 12 would change
rewindagents rewind 12 --only src/db.py   # take back just that file
rescue: rewindagents summary          # which files are different now, by how much, and which steps did it
rewindagents revert 7         # take back step 7 alone, keep every later step and hand edit
rewindagents rewind 0         # put every file back as it was before the session's first step
rescue_says: Three commands, in the order you need them.

`rewind` and `revert` refuse, change nothing and exit 1 when they would overwrite a change made after the agent's step (your own edit, for example); the message names the file and the command that shows what would be lost.
Every rewind is itself a step, so it can be undone, and it prints the command that undoes it.

status: rewindagents status             # per agent config file: ok, STALE, FAILING, partial or no hook; then the log and the store
status_says: After the hooks come this project's log: how many records it holds, when the last one was written, and whether the chain verifies; then the store: how much disk `.rewindagents/` takes.

Each hook that is in place is also run once, the way the agent runs it, in a new temporary folder, and must write a record there: one that runs but records nothing (a broken install the stale check cannot see) is `FAILING`, with the hook's own error message, and `status` exits 1.
A hook is stale when its interpreter path or its `PYTHONPATH` directory no longer exists; `status` then exits 1.
ui_says: A local page over the log.
Click a step, or move with `j` / `k`, to see each file's diff and the step's input and result (`d` hides or shows the diffs).
It listens on 127.0.0.1 only, on a free port unless you pass `--port`.
The link it prints carries a random token made for this run; every request without it gets a 403, and so does any request whose Host header is not 127.0.0.1 or localhost on that port.
Rewinds are POST only and must come from the page itself.
No fonts, scripts or images are fetched from anywhere, so it works offline.
